question.worked_solution:
Let $y=\operatorname{tanh}⁡{x}^{2}.$ Note that $f(x)$ is a one-to-one function on $x\ge 0.$ We have $y\in [0,1)$ for $x\in [0,\infty ).$ 

To find the inverse function we swap $x$ and $y:$ 

$$
x=\operatorname{tanh}⁡{y}^{2},
$$

where $x\in [0,1)$ and $y\in [0,\infty ).$

Next, we apply the definition of $\operatorname{tanh}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{e}^{2{y}^{2}}-1}{{e}^{2{y}^{2}}+1} \\ x({e}^{2{y}^{2}}+1) & ={e}^{2{y}^{2}}-1 \\ (x-1){e}^{2{y}^{2}} & +(x+1)=0\end{aligned}
$$

Isolating the ${e}^{2{y}^{2}}$ term, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{2{y}^{2}} & =-\frac{x+1}{x-1} \\ {e}^{2{y}^{2}} & =\frac{1+x}{1-x} \\ 2{y}^{2} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1+x}{1-x}) \\ {y}^{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1+x}{1-x}) \\ y & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1+x}{1-x})}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $y\ge 0,$ we select the positive root. Therefore,

$$
y=\sqrt{\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1+x}{1-x})}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\sqrt{\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1+x}{1-x})}.
$$
